annotation.title_clean: Cognitive Incompatibilities Between Law and Robotic Legal-Decision Making
annotation.title_en: Cognitive Incompatibilities Between Law and Robotic Legal-Decision Making
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 311 (Robophilosophy 2018 / TRANSOR 2018), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper (Robophilosophy 2018) comparing robotic and human legal decision-making. It argues people cannot relate to robot decision-makers, which undermines perceived fairness and trust in the legal system, creating cognitive incompatibilities between law and robotics. Only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: Identical legal decisions by a robot and a human differ in how fairness is perceived.
People can relate to human decision-makers but not to robots.
Reproducing relatability in robots is unforeseeable given current cognitive science.
Robot legal decisions would not recreate trust in the fairness of the legal system.
